before.whatWasWrong: The headline came from a sensor 22 miles away. No travel time, no soaking loss into the sand, no depth at this road was in that rule. The county's own report, from the crossing itself, was demoted below it, and its direction was never fetched.

after.summary: County says Proceed with Caution: Avra Valley Rd west of the Brawley Wash, eastbound (updated 11/01/26, 11:48). That is the county reporting this road, not a measurement of how deep the water is. No local rain, weather alert or flood model shows water at this road right now.

after.whyThisReads: The county's report leads, in its own words, with which way it applies to and when it was last touched. The upstream numbers are still there, with how far away each sensor is and a plain statement that they do not give a depth or an arrival time here. The crossing is not called clear.

stillUnknown: Whether any of that upstream water reaches this dip, when, and how deep. No rating curve, travel time or channel-loss figure exists for this crossing.
There is still no sensor at the crossing. That is the real fix (docs/PERMISSION.md).
500 cfs is still a round number; it now only decides when a reading is called a big flow.
Straight-line miles are not channel miles.
The county's note is as old as its timestamp: 11:48 AM against a 20:04 reading.
